note: 나눠요 in polite speech.

ex.en: Shall we split the pizza in half?
I had a chat with my coworkers.
We'll split into two teams.
I ordered it online.
Class is online today.
They sell it cheaper online.

note: ㅂ-irregular: 아름다워요. Often for scenery; 예쁘다 is more casual.

ex.en: The ocean is really beautiful.
The bride was so beautiful.
The lyrics of this song are beautiful.
I got a good opportunity at work.
Let's go together next time.
I hope I get a chance to go to Korea.

note: 아무도 + negative = nobody; 아무거나 = anything at all.

ex.en: There's nobody home.
Anything is fine with me.
Call me anytime.
This restaurant has a wide menu.
This store has lots of different colors.

ex.s: 우리 학교에는 다양한 나라 학생들이 있어요.
ex.en: Our school has students from many countries.

note: 줄(을) 서다 = to stand in line.

ex.en: I stood in line for 30 minutes.
I was standing the whole time on the bus.
I'll take a photo. Stand over there.

note: Casual; add 요 for polite speech: 그래요.

ex.en: Okay, see you tomorrow.
Really? I didn't know.
Sure, let's go together.

note: For begging or strong wishes; ordinary requests use -아/어 주세요.

ex.en: Please, be quiet.

ex.s: 제발 내일은 비가 안 왔으면 좋겠어요.
ex.en: I really hope it doesn't rain tomorrow.
Please don't be late.

note: For elders or superiors. 안녕히 계세요 = goodbye (to someone staying).

ex.en: Is your mother at home?
The team leader isn't in right now.
My grandmother is in Busan.

note: 참! at the start = "Oh, right!" when remembering something.

ex.en: The weather is really nice.
The food is really delicious.
Oh right, there's a meeting tomorrow.
This milk tastes a bit weird.
My phone is acting a bit weird.
The weather is strange today.

note: 선물하다 = to give a gift.

ex.en: Thanks for the birthday present!
I'm going to the department store to buy Mom a gift.
This is a gift I brought back from Korea.

note: Use native numbers: 한 장, 두 장. For tickets, photos, paper.

ex.en: Two tickets, please.
Could you take a photo of us?
How many sheets of paper do you need?

note: 엄마 is casual; 어머님 is more respectful, e.g., for someone else's mother.

ex.en: My mother is a good cook.
I called my mother yesterday.
Where does your mother live, Ji-woo?

note: Also 시장 = mayor (a different word, same spelling).

ex.en: I bought fruit at the market.
This market is famous for tteokbokki.
The market is close to my house.
I'll definitely keep my promise.
Please be on time for work.
You have to follow the school rules.

note: Casual speech only; use 네 in polite speech.

ex.en: Yeah, got it.
Yeah, I'm home now.
Yeah, it's really good.

note: 돌아와요 in polite speech.

ex.en: What time are you coming back?
I got back from my trip yesterday.
I'll be right back.
Today is a special day.
Do you have any special plans this weekend?
The kimchi at this place tastes special.
Have you decided what to eat?
We decided to move.

ex.s: 어떤 걸 살지 아직 결정 못 했어요.
ex.en: I haven't decided which one to buy yet.
Is there a convenience store around here?
There are a lot of good restaurants around the hotel.
A lot of people around me work out.
I'm really interested in Korean history.
This restaurant has a long history.
History class is the most fun.

note: N 대신 = instead of N.

ex.en: I'll have tea instead of coffee.
I'll go instead today.
I took the bus instead of the subway.
The hospital has a lot of patients today.
My father has diabetes.
The nurse called the patient's name.

note: Also 초 = candle (a different word).

ex.en: Please wait just 10 seconds.
Microwave it for 30 seconds.
I'm moving at the beginning of next month.

en: to take out, leave out; lose (weight)
note: N 빼고 = except N.

ex.en: No cucumber, please.
Everyone's here except Minho.
I need to lose some weight.

note: Takes 을/를; 싫다 is the adjective (N이 싫어요).

ex.en: I don't like spicy food.
Our cat hates baths.
My younger sibling hates math.

note: 르-irregular: 빨라요. Adverb: 빨리.

ex.en: The subway is faster than the bus.
The internet here is really fast.
Delivery was faster than I expected.
This is my favorite author.
That writer's new book is out.
Wei is a webtoon artist.

note: Passive 막히다: 길이 막혀요 = traffic is jammed.

ex.en: A car is blocking the road.
Cover your mouth when you cough.
Mom stopped us from going.

note: 기억하다 = to remember; 기억(이) 나다 = to come to mind.

ex.en: I don't really remember that time.
I have lots of good memories here.
Do you remember my name?

note: For skill level, 실력 is often more natural.

ex.en: Minho is really capable.
That's beyond my abilities.

ex.s: 다음 주에 한국어 능력 시험을 봐요.
ex.en: I'm taking the Korean proficiency test next week.
I made it myself.
Let's talk in person.
I went to the store and bought it in person.
I go to church every Sunday.
I ate with friends from church.
There are many churches near our house.

en: to fall into; (weight, hair) come off
note: 살이 빠지다 = to lose weight; 사랑에 빠지다 = to fall in love.

ex.en: My phone fell in the water.
The two of them fell in love.
You've lost a lot of weight!
I watch the news every morning.
The news says it'll rain tomorrow.
I read the news on my phone.

note: Two words with the same spelling: street and distance.

ex.en: There are a lot of people on the street.
There are lots of cafes on this street.
It's within walking distance.

note: 남동생 = younger brother; 여동생 = younger sister.

ex.en: I have two younger siblings.
I live with my younger sibling.
My younger sibling is a college student.

en: to end up; what to do (어쩌죠?)
note: Short for 어찌하다. 어쩌다가 as an adverb also means "by chance."

ex.en: How did you get hurt?
What do we do now?
Somehow I ended up being late.

note: 그림을 그리다 = to draw a picture.

ex.en: Who drew this picture?
I take drawing lessons every weekend.
The child drew a picture of Mom.

note: 축구하다 = to play soccer.

ex.en: I play soccer with friends on weekends.
Did you watch the soccer game yesterday?
My son is learning soccer at school.

note: Everyday "run" is often 뛰다. Homonym 달리다 = to hang, be attached.

ex.en: I run in the park every morning.
I ran to catch the bus.
The train goes really fast.

note: Goes before a noun (새 차). The adjective is 새롭다.

ex.en: I bought a new car!
Are those new shoes? They're pretty.
The new semester has started.

note: 나빠요 (ㅡ drops). 나쁘지 않아요 = not bad.

ex.en: The weather is bad today.
Smoking is bad for your health.
This restaurant isn't bad.

note: Politer than 싸다; common in shops and ads.

ex.en: This store is cheaper.
The lunch menu here is reasonably priced.
I'm looking for an inexpensive hotel.

note: A filler while thinking.

ex.en: Hmm... I'm not sure.
Mmm, this is tasty!
Hmm, how about next week?
What role does that actor play?
My job is to prepare the meetings.
Dad plays a big role at home.
The wind is strong today.
This coffee is a bit strong.
My mom is a really strong person.

note: 잊어버리다 is very common in speech. 잊지 마세요 = don't forget.

ex.en: Don't forget your umbrella.
I forgot my password.
I'll never forget that day.
The whole store is on sale.
The whole team went to the work dinner.
Please show me the full menu.
Let's meet at 3 p.m.
They say it'll rain in the afternoon.
Are you free this afternoon?
Forget the past.
I wish I could go back in time.
The Korean past tense is hard.

note: 부탁해요 / 부탁드려요 (more polite) = please.

ex.en: Can I ask you a favor?
I look forward to working with you.
I asked my friend to help me move.
Did you understand what I said?
Sorry, I didn't understand.
I understand how you feel.

note: 뜻 is more common for word meanings.

ex.en: What does this word mean?
This gift means a lot to me.
There's no point doing it this way.
I found a nice cafe.
I found an error in the report.
I found a wallet in the park.

note: Spoken form of 이야기하다.

ex.en: Let's talk later.
Did you tell Mom?
I talked with my friend all night.
Don't leave any food.
Please leave a message.
Save some cake for me too.

note: N밖에 + negative = only N (e.g., 천 원밖에 없어요).

ex.en: It's raining outside.
I'll wait outside.
Let's eat out today.

note: Also 총 = gun (a different word).

ex.en: How much is it in total?
There are five of us in total.
It takes two hours in total to Seoul.

note: Used for online reviews; 리뷰 is also common.

ex.en: I came to this restaurant after reading reviews.
This product has good reviews.
I posted a write-up of my trip on my blog.

note: 그려요 in polite speech.

ex.en: The child is drawing a picture.
Please draw me a map.
I paint landscapes in the park every weekend.

note: 차이(가) 나다 = to differ; 나이 차이 = age gap.

ex.en: What's the difference between the two?
There's a big price difference.
There's a three-year age gap between us.
This chair is a bit low.
The temperature is low today.
My score was lower than I expected.

note: Casual; politely use 안녕하세요, or 안녕히 가세요/계세요 for goodbye.

ex.en: Hi, how have you been?
Bye! See you tomorrow.
Hi, Ji-woo!
We know each other well.
Coworkers should help each other.
The two of them love each other.
I take a walk in the park every evening.
I went to the park with my dog.
Is there a park around here?
What drama are you watching these days?
This drama is really good.
I learn Korean by watching dramas.
There isn't much space in the room.
Is there room in the car for luggage?
This cafe is spacious.
What time does the show start?
Last night's performance was really good.
I bought two tickets for the show.

note: 1억 = 100,000,000; 10억 = one billion.

ex.en: This apartment costs 500 million won.
Homes in Seoul cost hundreds of millions of won.
The world population is over 8 billion.

note: -(으)ㄹ 예정이에요 = I plan to / it's scheduled to.

ex.en: I'm planning to move next month.
The flight is scheduled to arrive at 3.
The wedding is planned for June.

note: 자유롭다 = to be free.

ex.en: Living alone is nice because I have freedom.
There's free time in the afternoon.
Coming to the work dinner is optional.
What's the purpose of your visit?
The goal of this trip is to rest.
What's your goal in working out?

note: 옆집 = next door.

ex.en: There's a cafe next to the bank.
Sit next to me.
The person next door is kind.

note: 포함하다 = to include.

ex.en: Is breakfast included?
Shipping is included in the price.

ex.s: 그 명단에 제 이름도 포함돼 있어요?
ex.en: Is my name on that list too?

note: 맛있다 = delicious; 맛없다 = not tasty.

ex.en: How does it taste?
What flavor is this ice cream?
Mom's kimchi tastes the best.

note: Short for 재미있다; very common in speech.

ex.en: Was that movie good?
Studying Korean is fun.
Minho is a really funny person.

note: Honorific/humble form of 말. 말씀하세요 = please go ahead.

ex.en: I've heard a lot about you.
Yes, go ahead.
Dad is right.

en: to set, adjust; match; be on time
note: To guess an answer correctly is 맞히다 (often confused).

ex.en: I set the alarm for 7.
I'll be there on time.
My friend and I wore matching outfits.
Science class is my favorite.
My son likes science.
Shall we go to the science museum this weekend?

note: 술 한잔해요 = let's grab a drink.

ex.en: Want to grab a drink tonight?
I can't drink alcohol.

ex.s: 약 먹을 때는 술 마시지 마세요.
ex.en: Don't drink alcohol while taking medicine.

note: Softens a question or request.

ex.en: Excuse me, where's the restroom?
Are you free today, by any chance?
If it happens to rain, I'll let you know.

note: Also "to save (someone)".

ex.en: I'm looking for a job these days.
It's hard to find a place to live in Seoul.
I barely managed to get tickets for the show.
My computer is slow again.
I play computer games on weekends.
My work computer broke down.

note: 전 is shorter and more common. Homonym 이전 = relocation.

ex.en: The previous version was better.
I like it here better than my previous company.
Have we met before?
I dropped my phone on the ground.
My grandfather has land in the countryside.
The ground is wet from the rain.
That person's behavior is a bit strange.
Actions matter more than words.
The child's behavior has improved a lot.
What do you want to do in the future?
I'm saving money for the future.
Nobody knows the future.
I'm presenting at the meeting tomorrow.
I gave a presentation in English in class.
When do they announce the test results?

note: ㅂ-irregular: 무서워요. Means both "scary" and "I'm scared."

ex.en: This movie is so scary.
I get scared when I'm alone at night.
Our teacher is a little scary.
I joined this company because the terms were good.
This place has everything I want.
There's one condition.
There are too many ads on YouTube.
I like the song in this ad.
I bought it after seeing an ad.
Let's eat first and then talk.
I'll head home for now.
Just give it a try first.

note: 검사(를) 받다 = to get tested. Homonym 검사 = prosecutor.

ex.en: I'm getting a blood test tomorrow.
The test results are good.
They checked my bag at the airport.

en: as it is, the same, exactly

ex.en: Just leave it as it is.
You look the same as 10 years ago.
I made it exactly by the recipe.

note: 인사하다 = to greet; 인사드리다 is the humble form.

ex.en: I said hello to my neighbor.
The new employee came by to say hello.
The child greets Grandma nicely.
Let's go to the beach in summer.
Summer in Korea is really hot.
What are you doing this summer vacation?

note: 정신(이) 없다 = hectic, frazzled; 정신 차리다 = to pull yourself together.

ex.en: I'm so busy lately, I'm frazzled.

ex.s: 아침에 정신이 없어서 지갑을 놓고 왔어요.
ex.en: I was so frazzled this morning, I left my wallet.
Stay alert when you're driving.
